kidCareers.name: Electrical Engineer

In Ohio alone, the push toward EVs, semiconductors, and renewable energy has made electrical engineering one of the highest-demand fields right now.
dailyWork: Design circuit schematics and printed circuit boards (PCBs)
Run simulations in SPICE or similar tools
Build and test prototypes on a workbench
Collaborate with mechanical, software, and hardware engineers

Tri-C Associate in Electrical/Electronic Engineering Technology — or transfer-ready courses
CSU Bachelor's in Electrical Engineering (BSEE)

kidCareers.outlook: Steady demand; growing in climate / private-sector roles.
pathways: Bachelor's in Atmospheric Science or Physics
Master's for research or forecasting leadership

kidCareers.name: Architect
kidCareers.tagline: Design the buildings and spaces people live, work, and learn in.
kidCareers.description: Architects blend art, engineering, and human factors to design spaces. Strong in both commercial and residential markets; growing demand for sustainable and adaptive-reuse design.
dailyWork: Sketch and build 3D models of buildings
Meet with clients to understand needs
kidCareers.outlook: Steady demand; especially strong in urban revitalization (Cleveland is booming).
pathways: Tri-C Architecture / Construction Technology
Accredited Master's of Architecture (usually 5–7 years total)
Licensure exam (ARE) + experience

kidCareers.name: Electrician
kidCareers.tagline: Wire the buildings, factories, and grids that keep the lights on.
kidCareers.description: Electricians install and repair the wiring inside homes, hospitals, factories, and data centers. Cleveland's hospital systems (Cleveland Clinic, UH), Sherwin-Williams' new HQ, and Intel's Licking County build mean steady demand for years.
dailyWork: Pull wire, install conduit, mount panels
kidCareers.outlook: Strong, long-term — every new building needs electricians and Ohio's apprentice pipeline is paid from day one.
pathways: Take CTE electrical at a career-tech high school
Apply to an IBEW Local 38 or NECA apprenticeship (4 years, paid)
Earn journeyman license, then master electrician

kidCareers.name: Plumber
kidCareers.tagline: Install and repair the water, gas, and waste systems people depend on every day.
kidCareers.description: Plumbers run water lines, gas lines, and drain systems in homes and businesses — and fix them when something goes wrong. Master plumbers in Cleveland can earn six figures and run their own shop.
dailyWork: Cut and join pipe (copper, PEX, PVC)
Use camera scopes to inspect sewer lines
kidCareers.outlook: Steady — every building has plumbing, and there's a shortage of journeyman plumbers nationwide.
pathways: CTE Plumbing at a career-tech high school
5-year paid Plumbers Local 55 apprenticeship in Cleveland
State of Ohio journeyman license

kidCareers.name: HVAC Technician
kidCareers.tagline: Install and service heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning systems.
kidCareers.description: HVAC techs keep buildings comfortable — homes, schools, hospitals, factories. With heat pumps and refrigeration becoming more efficient, demand is rising across Cleveland's housing and commercial market.
dailyWork: Install furnaces, AC units, heat pumps
kidCareers.outlook: Strong growth — heat-pump retrofits and commercial cooling are expanding faster than the trade can train techs.
pathways: CTE HVAC at a career-tech high school
Tri-C HVAC Associate (or paid apprenticeship)
EPA 608 refrigerant certification
State of Ohio HVAC contractor license (after experience)

kidCareers.name: Welder
kidCareers.tagline: Fuse metal for bridges, ships, pipelines, race cars, and skyscrapers.
kidCareers.description: Welders join metal using heat — MIG, TIG, stick, and more. Ohio's steel, auto, aerospace, and shipbuilding industries all need them. Certified pipe welders working overtime can clear six figures.
dailyWork: Set up and run MIG, TIG, or stick rigs
Cut metal with torch or plasma
kidCareers.outlook: Steady and well-paid — pipe welders and underwater welders are in particularly short supply.
pathways: CTE welding at a career-tech high school
Tri-C Welding Certificate (Associate optional)
AWS certification, then specialty (pipe, structural, robotic)

kidCareers.name: Carpenter
kidCareers.tagline: Build the frames, decks, cabinets, and trim that buildings are made of.
kidCareers.description: Carpenters frame houses, build decks, install cabinets, and finish trim. There are residential, commercial, and specialty paths (cabinetmaking, scenic carpentry, finish work). Cleveland's housing market keeps demand steady.
dailyWork: Square, level, and plumb every connection
Train apprentices on safe tool use
kidCareers.outlook: Steady — every building needs carpenters, and finish carpentry stays in demand even in slow markets.
pathways: CTE carpentry at career-tech
Carpenters Local 1750 apprenticeship (Cleveland)
Journeyman → finish/specialty work or self-employment

kidCareers.name: Diesel Mechanic
kidCareers.tagline: Keep trucks, buses, and heavy equipment running.
kidCareers.description: Diesel mechanics fix the trucks that move America's goods — and the bulldozers, generators, and farm equipment that build and feed it. Cleveland's logistics corridor (Norfolk Southern, NS Container Yard) and Ohio's farms keep demand strong.
dailyWork: Diagnose engine + transmission problems with scan tools
Rebuild engines, replace turbos, swap injectors
kidCareers.outlook: Strong — the trucking industry has a chronic mechanic shortage and pays well to keep good techs.
pathways: CTE auto/diesel at career-tech high school
Tri-C Diesel Power Technology Associate
ASE Master Medium/Heavy Truck certifications

kidCareers.name: Automotive Technician
kidCareers.tagline: Diagnose and repair the cars and trucks that move people every day.
kidCareers.description: Auto techs do everything from oil changes to engine rebuilds to EV battery work. With Ford and Honda building EV plants in Ohio and battery sites coming, EV-trained techs are increasingly in demand.
dailyWork: Service hybrid and EV battery systems
Estimate repair time and cost for service writers
kidCareers.outlook: Steady; EV-certified techs are growing fastest as Cleveland-area dealers and fleets electrify.
pathways: CTE Auto Tech at career-tech high school
Tri-C Automotive Technology Associate
ASE certifications (Master Automobile Technician)
EV-specific manufacturer training

kidCareers.name: Machinist
kidCareers.tagline: Run the precision machines that make every part in modern manufacturing.
kidCareers.description: Machinists set up and operate CNC mills and lathes that cut metal to thousandths of an inch. Cleveland's aerospace (NASA Glenn, GE Aviation), automotive, and precision-parts manufacturers all need them.
dailyWork: Program CNC mills and lathes from CAD models
Troubleshoot tool wear and surface finish
kidCareers.outlook: Strong — Ohio's manufacturing job openings outpace machinist apprentice graduations.
pathways: CTE precision machining
Tri-C CNC + Manufacturing Associate
Specialty certifications (NIMS, Mastercam)

kidCareers.name: Physical Therapist
kidCareers.tagline: Help people recover from injury, surgery, or chronic pain so they can move again.
kidCareers.description: PTs work with patients recovering from sports injuries, car accidents, strokes, joint replacements, and chronic conditions. Cleveland Clinic, UH, and MetroHealth all have large rehabilitation programs.
dailyWork: Evaluate strength, balance, and range of motion
Use manual therapy and modalities (ultrasound, e-stim)
Educate patients and families on home exercises
kidCareers.outlook: Strong long-term growth as the population ages and outpatient rehab expands.
pathways: Bachelor's in Exercise Science, Kinesiology, or Biology
3-year Doctor of Physical Therapy (DPT) — required
State licensure + clinical residency for specialties

kidCareers.name: Dental Hygienist
kidCareers.tagline: Clean teeth, take X-rays, and teach patients how to keep their smiles healthy.
kidCareers.description: Hygienists spend most of the appointment with the patient — cleaning, screening for problems, taking imaging, and coaching brushing/flossing habits. Cleveland-area dental practices are hiring constantly.
dailyWork: Take dental X-rays and intra-oral photos
Screen for gum disease and oral cancers
kidCareers.outlook: Steady — preventive dentistry continues to grow.
pathways: Tri-C Dental Hygiene Associate (selective admission)
Pass National + Ohio licensure exams
Optional Bachelor's for teaching/research roles

kidCareers.name: Veterinarian
kidCareers.tagline: Diagnose, treat, and operate on animals — from goldfish to draft horses.
kidCareers.description: Vets work in small-animal clinics, on farms with livestock, at zoos, or in wildlife rehabilitation. The Ohio State College of Veterinary Medicine is the closest accredited DVM program.
dailyWork: Diagnose using imaging, bloodwork, and physical exam
Counsel pet owners on nutrition + prevention
kidCareers.outlook: Steady — animal medicine expands as pet ownership grows.
pathways: Strong bio + chem in high school
Bachelor's (pre-vet/biology/animal science)
4-year Doctor of Veterinary Medicine (DVM) — OSU is closest
Optional internships + specialty residency

kidCareers.name: Pharmacist
kidCareers.tagline: Dispense medications safely, counsel patients, and catch drug interactions.
kidCareers.description: Pharmacists work in retail pharmacies, hospitals, mail-order, or specialty (cancer, transplant). Ohio Northern, OSU, and U Cincinnati host PharmD programs; Cleveland Clinic and University Hospitals employ hundreds.
dailyWork: Counsel patients on drug interactions + side effects
Work with physicians on therapy choices
kidCareers.outlook: Stable — clinical pharmacy and specialty pharmacy continue to expand.
pathways: Strong chemistry + biology in high school
Bachelor's in biology, chem, or pre-pharmacy
4-year Doctor of Pharmacy (PharmD)
Optional 1–2 year residency for clinical roles

kidCareers.name: Paramedic / EMT
kidCareers.tagline: Respond to emergencies and keep patients alive en route to the hospital.
kidCareers.description: EMTs and paramedics provide life-saving care on ambulances, fire departments, and at major events. Cleveland EMS, fire departments across NE Ohio, and hospital transport services all hire continuously.
dailyWork: Assess patients on scene (trauma, cardiac, OB)
Document calls and brief ER staff
kidCareers.outlook: Strong demand — every department is short-staffed.
pathways: EMT-Basic certificate (3–6 months)
Tri-C Paramedic Associate (1–2 years)
Optional fire academy + dual fire/medic certification

kidCareers.name: Firefighter
kidCareers.tagline: Respond to fires, accidents, and emergencies — and keep your community safe.
kidCareers.description: Firefighters run into burning buildings, respond to car accidents, treat medical emergencies, and teach fire safety. Most NE Ohio firefighters are also paramedics. Cleveland Division of Fire and dozens of suburban departments hire from civil-service lists.
dailyWork: Respond to fire, EMS, and rescue calls
Train for high-angle, water, and confined-space rescue
Inspect commercial properties for fire-code compliance
Teach kids fire safety at schools
kidCareers.outlook: Steady, very competitive — lots of applicants for limited openings, but jobs are stable for life.
pathways: Fire Academy + EMT certification (some HS programs offer it)
Optional Associate in Fire Science
Pass civil-service exam + agility test

kidCareers.name: Police Officer
kidCareers.tagline: Patrol, investigate, and serve the community as a sworn officer.
kidCareers.description: Patrol officers respond to 911 calls, investigate crimes, and build community relationships. Detectives focus on investigations. Cleveland Division of Police, county sheriffs, and dozens of suburban departments hire annually.
dailyWork: Patrol assigned beat by car or foot
Take statements, write reports, gather evidence
kidCareers.outlook: Steady, very competitive — agencies are working to recruit more applicants.
pathways: Ohio Peace Officer Training Academy (OPOTA) — 700+ hours
Optional Associate or Bachelor's in Criminal Justice
Pass background, polygraph, psych, agility

kidCareers.name: Elementary Teacher
kidCareers.tagline: Teach reading, math, science, and social studies to grades K-5.
kidCareers.description: Elementary teachers shape kids' love of learning — and Ohio has a serious teacher shortage in many subjects. CMSD and suburban districts across NE Ohio are hiring constantly, with signing bonuses in some areas.
dailyWork: Plan and deliver lessons across subjects
Assess student work and give feedback
Collaborate with grade-level team and specialists
kidCareers.outlook: Strong demand statewide — Ohio has hundreds of unfilled teaching positions every year.
pathways: Bachelor's in Elementary Education (4 years)
Pass Ohio teaching exams (OAE)
Optional Master's for higher pay band

kidCareers.name: Social Worker
kidCareers.tagline: Connect kids, families, and adults to services that help them thrive.
kidCareers.description: Social workers serve in schools, hospitals, foster care, mental-health clinics, and county agencies. Cuyahoga County Children & Family Services, MetroHealth, and Frontline Service all hire continuously.
dailyWork: Connect families to housing, food, mental-health resources
Investigate child welfare cases (if in protective services)
Provide counseling for individuals and families
Document case work in compliance systems
kidCareers.outlook: Steady, growing — county systems and behavioral-health providers continually need licensed staff.
pathways: Bachelor's in Social Work (BSW)
Master's in Social Work (MSW) for clinical roles
LSW / LISW Ohio licensure

kidCareers.name: Accountant
kidCareers.tagline: Track money, prepare taxes, and audit the books that keep businesses honest.
kidCareers.description: Accountants work in public accounting firms (PwC, Deloitte, Plante Moran in Cleveland), corporate finance, government, or as CPAs running their own practice. Strong job security and a clear path to six figures with the CPA license.
dailyWork: Prepare individual and business tax returns
kidCareers.outlook: Steady — accounting is consistently in demand.
pathways: Bachelor's in Accounting (4 years)
CPA exam + 150 credit hours (often a Master's of Accountancy)
Tax-specialty or audit-specialty roles after a few years

kidCareers.name: Marketing Manager
kidCareers.tagline: Design campaigns that tell a brand's story and bring in new customers.
kidCareers.description: Marketing managers run digital ads, design email campaigns, build content strategies, and analyze what works. Sherwin-Williams, KeyBank, Progressive, and Cleveland Cavaliers all run large marketing teams.
dailyWork: Plan digital, social, and email campaigns
Brief creative teams and approve assets
Analyze campaign performance in Google Analytics + dashboards
kidCareers.outlook: Steady; digital marketing roles grow fastest.
pathways: Bachelor's in Marketing, Communications, or Business
Entry-level coordinator → senior specialist → manager
Optional MBA for senior brand roles

kidCareers.name: Financial Analyst
kidCareers.tagline: Help companies and investors decide where to put their money.
kidCareers.description: Financial analysts build models, forecast performance, and recommend investments. KeyBank, Sherwin-Williams, Parker Hannifin, and the federal Cleveland Fed Reserve Bank are major employers.
dailyWork: Forecast revenue, costs, and cash flow
kidCareers.outlook: Steady; data-driven finance is one of the fastest-growing analyst tracks.
pathways: Bachelor's in Finance, Economics, or Accounting
Optional CFA certification (3 exams over 2+ years)
Entry analyst → senior → portfolio manager

kidCareers.name: Graphic Designer
kidCareers.tagline: Design the logos, posters, websites, and packaging the world sees.
kidCareers.description: Graphic designers work at ad agencies, in-house brand teams, freelance studios, or major employers like Sherwin-Williams, American Greetings (the giant card company is in Westlake), and Cleveland Clinic.
dailyWork: Sketch ideas, then iterate in Adobe Illustrator/Photoshop
Lay out posters, brochures, web graphics
Present work to clients + take feedback
Prep files for print and digital production
kidCareers.outlook: Steady; digital design and motion graphics grow fastest.
pathways: Build a portfolio in high school
Tri-C Visual Communication & Design Associate
CSU Bachelor's of Arts in Graphic Design

kidCareers.name: Animator / 3D Artist
kidCareers.tagline: Bring characters, products, and worlds to life — in games, film, and ads.
kidCareers.description: Animators and 3D artists work in games (indie + AAA), film studios, ad agencies, architecture viz, and biomedical animation. Tools include Maya, Blender, ZBrush, Unreal Engine, and After Effects.
dailyWork: Composite frames in After Effects or Nuke
kidCareers.outlook: Growing — especially game, biomedical, and AR/VR roles.
pathways: Build a demo reel in high school
CSU Bachelor's in Animation or Studio Art
Optional Master's for film/AAA studio work

kidCareers.name: Journalist / Reporter
kidCareers.tagline: Investigate, write, and report the stories that hold institutions accountable.
kidCareers.description: Journalists work for newspapers (Plain Dealer), TV/radio (Ideastream, WKYC), online (Axios Cleveland, Signal Cleveland), and nonprofits. Investigative work pays the most; entry roles are competitive.
dailyWork: Interview sources on the phone or in person
Write articles or scripts under deadline
kidCareers.outlook: Tight but local + investigative roles are growing as nonprofit news expands.
pathways: Write for HS newspaper / podcast / YouTube
Bachelor's in Journalism, English, or Comms
Internships at local outlets

kidCareers.name: Chef
kidCareers.tagline: Design menus and lead the kitchen at restaurants, hotels, and catering.
kidCareers.description: Chefs run kitchens at restaurants, hotels, hospitals, schools, and corporate cafeterias. Cleveland's restaurant scene (Lola/Mabel's, Edwins, Crop Bistro) has launched many career chefs.
kidCareers.outlook: Steady — chefs with strong management skills move up fast.
pathways: Start in a working kitchen as soon as you can
Tri-C Hospitality Management / Culinary Arts Associate
Externship + management track

kidCareers.name: Farmer / Ranch Manager
kidCareers.tagline: Grow crops or raise livestock — running a business outdoors.
kidCareers.description: Ohio is the 9th-largest agricultural state in the US. Crops (corn, soybeans, wheat), dairy, beef, and poultry are major. Modern farms use GPS-guided tractors, drone scouting, and precision irrigation.
dailyWork: Plant, scout, and harvest crops by season
Care for livestock (feeding, breeding, vet care)
Sell at markets, to co-ops, or to processors
kidCareers.outlook: Stable; precision-ag and specialty crops are growing fastest.
pathways: FFA + 4-H in high school
Ohio State ATI (Wooster) Associate in Agriculture
OSU Bachelor's in Agriculture

kidCareers.name: Park Ranger
kidCareers.tagline: Protect and teach in state, national, and metro parks.
kidCareers.description: Rangers patrol parks, help visitors, lead education programs, and enforce wildlife rules. Cleveland Metroparks and Cuyahoga Valley National Park are major NE Ohio employers.
dailyWork: Respond to lost hikers or wildlife issues
Enforce park rules and wildlife regs
kidCareers.outlook: Stable; very competitive — federal jobs especially.
pathways: Bachelor's in Wildlife Bio, Forestry, Env. Science, or Parks Mgmt
Seasonal ranger / interpreter work
Pass federal background and physical for full-time

kidCareers.name: Airline Pilot
kidCareers.tagline: Fly commercial passenger or cargo aircraft.
kidCareers.description: Airline pilots fly for regional + major carriers. Hopkins Airport (Cleveland) is a United hub. The path is expensive but pay reaches $200k+ at majors; cargo pilots have similar earnings.
kidCareers.outlook: Strong — pilot shortage continues for both regional + major airlines.
pathways: Private Pilot License (PPL) in HS or early college
Build hours toward 1500-hour ATP minimum
Optional Bachelor's in Aviation or Engineering
Regional airline first job → major carrier

kidCareers.name: Truck Driver (CDL)
kidCareers.tagline: Move freight across Ohio and the country with a commercial license.
kidCareers.description: Truck drivers move everything from groceries to construction materials. NE Ohio's logistics corridor (I-90, I-71, I-80) plus rail yards mean steady work. Local routes pay less; OTR (over-the-road) pays more.
dailyWork: Drive routes safely + meet delivery windows
kidCareers.outlook: Strong demand — the industry has a chronic driver shortage.
pathways: CDL school (Class A) — typically 4–8 weeks
Pass CDL written + skills + driving exams
Start at carrier with on-the-job mentor

kidCareers.name: Electrical Lineman
kidCareers.tagline: Climb poles and bucket trucks to keep power flowing during storms and every day.
kidCareers.description: Linemen build and maintain the high-voltage lines that distribute electricity. FirstEnergy (Akron HQ) and rural electric co-ops in NE Ohio constantly need apprentices. Storm response can mean serious overtime pay.
dailyWork: Climb poles and operate bucket trucks
Switch and ground for safe work
kidCareers.outlook: Strong + well-paid — significant grid build-out + storm work.
pathways: CTE electrical or pre-apprentice program
Utility lineman apprenticeship (3–4 years, paid)
Journeyman lineman certification

kidCareers.name: Construction Manager
kidCareers.tagline: Run the schedule, budget, and crews on construction job sites.
kidCareers.description: Construction managers oversee everything from a townhouse build to a stadium. Major Cleveland projects (Browns stadium plans, Cleveland Clinic expansions, Intel-driven facilities) mean steady demand.
dailyWork: Walk job site for safety + quality checks
kidCareers.outlook: Strong — Ohio's commercial + infrastructure projects need PMs faster than schools graduate them.
pathways: Bachelor's in Construction Management or Civil Engineering
Work as estimator or assistant PM
PMP / OSHA-30 certifications for senior roles

kidCareers.name: Network Technician
kidCareers.tagline: Build and troubleshoot the networks that businesses, hospitals, and schools depend on.
kidCareers.description: Network technicians install and maintain switches, routers, firewalls, and Wi-Fi for businesses, hospitals, and schools. Cleveland-area employers (Cleveland Clinic IT, hospital systems, MSPs) hire steadily.
kidCareers.outlook: Strong; cybersecurity-adjacent network roles grow fastest.
pathways: Tri-C Network Engineering Associate
CompTIA Network+, then CCNA
Optional Bachelor's for senior architect roles

kidCareers.name: Psychologist
kidCareers.tagline: Help people understand their thoughts, emotions, and behaviors.
kidCareers.description: Clinical psychologists assess and treat mental-health conditions; school psychologists work with kids; research psychologists study cognition. Cleveland Clinic, UH, MetroHealth, and CMSD all have large psych staffs.
dailyWork: Write reports + consult with other clinicians
kidCareers.outlook: Strong — mental-health demand keeps climbing.
pathways: Bachelor's in Psychology
Doctorate (PhD or PsyD) for clinical practice — 5–7 years
Licensure exam + supervised hours
